resumen: A seated shoulder press where the dumbbells start in front of the face, palms facing you, and rotate as they rise until the palms face forward.
ejecucion: Sit on a bench with a backrest, with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, in front of your face and palms facing you.
Press up and, at the same time, open your elbows out to the sides and rotate your wrists.
At the top, arms almost straight and palms facing forward, without knocking the dumbbells together.
Lower by reversing the rotation until you are back at the start, keeping your back against the bench.
matices: We have found no study measuring the Arnold press itself. What has been measured is the shoulder press in general: seated, the anterior deltoid was somewhat more active with dumbbells than with a barbell; standing, somewhat less weight was also lifted. That the rotation adds work for the deltoid is the usual explanation, but it has not been tested.

fuentes.titulo: Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses
fuentes.autor: Saeterbakken and Fimland, J Strength Cond Res, 2013
